subject.title: Core hardening tracker: converge duplicated runtime invariants onto single owners

question: Which verified remaining ownership seam should be sponsored and sequenced next, with its permanent owner boundary agreed before implementation?
rationale: The tracker establishes real duplication, but the remaining rows cross distinct session, plugin/provider, error-policy, and agent-runtime owners; repository evidence cannot safely choose one blanket architecture or priority order.

options.title: Sponsor Bounded Rows
options.body: Keep the umbrella and approve individual rows only after reviewing their owner boundary, compatibility impact, and validation plan.

options.title: Narrow The Tracker
options.body: Retain only the highest-risk behavioral seams and move type-only or lower-priority cleanup into separate follow-ups.

options.title: Stop The Program
options.body: Close the umbrella and address future duplication only when a concrete user-facing regression establishes priority.

recommendation.title: Sponsor Bounded Rows
recommendation.body: Keep the umbrella and approve individual rows only after reviewing their owner boundary, compatibility impact, and validation plan.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged history spans the largest number of remaining decision surfaces, including subagent policy, tool behavior, provider routing, session projections, and attempt execution.
